facts.fact_text: The applicant explained that he had participated in a demonstration organised by his trade union on 1 May 2008 to celebrate International Labour Day.
At the material time, the applicant was a member of the local branch of the Tümbel-Sen trade union.

In April 2008, the KESK (Kamu Emekçileri Sendikaları Konfederasyonu – Confederation of Public Employees' Trade Unions) announced that it was planning a large-scale demonstration in Istanbul for 1 May 2008.
In May 2008, the applicant was informed that a disciplinary investigation had been initiated against him for being absent without leave on 1 May 2008.
The applicant was given a warning as a disciplinary sanction owing to his being absent without leave on 1 May 2008.
The disciplinary sanction of a warning was imposed on the applicant pursuant to section 125 of the Civil Servants Act (Law no. 657).
A full description of the relevant domestic law at the material time can be found in Karaçay v. Turkey (no. 6615/03, §§ 14-17, 27 March 2007).
A full description of the relevant domestic law at the material time can be found in İsmail Sezer v. Turkey (no. 36807/07, §§ 14-21, 24 March 2015).
